items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 5/28/2026). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only - no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI, female). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 3/2/2026 cardiology clinic visit. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc 372 ms), so the requirement was met within the window.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 2/12/2026 cardiology clinic visit. The start pre-dates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc 384 ms) - completed within the required time.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies: ECG within 30 days (due 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025 - within the window (it showed QTc 538 ms, which is separately flagged for QT review).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit; the revised memo (starts on/after 3/1/2026) requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, five days after the deadline, so the requirement was not met within the required time and remains overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 8/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so an ECG was required within 14 days (by 8/15/2026). No ECG has been recorded since 12/25/2025, so the post-start ECG is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 8/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit, requiring an ECG within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). No ECG exists anywhere in this patient's chart, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the 9/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit. The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been done since 3/9/2025, but the window has not yet closed at the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the follow-up is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Per the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days (by 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was resulted 9/5/2026, so the monitoring requirement was completed on time.

On 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (acting under the anticoagulation standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a clinic INR within 7 days (by 9/17/2026). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 8/22/2026; no INR has been resulted after the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

At the 7/15/2026 visit the note states the anticoagulant is being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but two overlapping anticoagulant orders were written minutes apart and are both still valid at the 9/24/2026 evaluation time: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7/15/2026-12/26/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (7/15/2026-12/25/2026). The note's own medication list shows both drugs. Two concurrent anticoagulants create a major bleeding risk and the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnosis 427.31, carried in every cardiology clinic note through 7/28/2026). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order has ever been active in the clinic record. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis = vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is remote and not documented as an active contraindication, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals with no organised P waves - at a ventricular rate of 134-136 bpm. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart entry needs correction and the rapid AF needs clinical review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) and prior embolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. No anticoagulant order is current as of 9/24/2026 (clinic notes list aspirin/statin only). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female). Her 3/14/2025 ECG shows sinus rhythm with a burst of irregular ectopy, consistent with paroxysmal AF. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent; thrombocytopenia is documented but no bleeding event, so this needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (latest 6/12/2026) and captured on ECG 108895765 (2/26/2025, AF at 150 bpm) and 101121040 (3/1/2025, AF). Current medications are famotidine and pantoprazole only; no anticoagulant is active. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (history of congestive/acute systolic heart failure with cardiomyopathy, hypertension), which meets the 2023 AF guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in a man. Needs review for initiation.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid to 12/28/2026) and the 8/20/2026 clinic note says 'continue current regimen', alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. A current anticoagulant with a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review requires prescriber review.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 8/22/2026-1/5/2027, watch-list drug). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm with frequent ectopy, ventricular rate 71, QT 540 ms, Bazett QTc 585 ms - well above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Last potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2/14/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes. She is also on warfarin. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are needed.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (started 11/10/2025, current order 7/29/2026-1/1/2027) plus warfarin. Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with QT 514 ms and Bazett QTc 538 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (4/20/2026) are normal. Amiodarone dose/continuation needs prescriber review with a repeat ECG.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily since 5/14/2024 (current order 4/23/2026-1/2/2027), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 471 ms and Bazett QTc 502 ms, at/above the 500 ms threshold (the 5/14/2024 note called the QT 'acceptable', which the measurement does not support). Potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (8/23/2025) are normal. Needs prescriber review and an up-to-date ECG.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily since 10/2/2023 (current order 5/29/2026-12/25/2026), a QT watch-list drug, at a dose above the recommended maximum for QT safety. Most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, QT 489 ms, Bazett QTc 530 ms - above the 500 ms threshold. Last potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026); no magnesium level is on file. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild rate variation; upright P in II/aVF, negative in aVR, PR 178 ms. Narrow QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +34 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 372 ms. No prior ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible. Consistent with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis +19 (normal), QT 326 ms and Bazett QTc 428 ms, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG 100698634 (6/20/2025) showed a regular sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm (upright P in I/II, negative in aVR) with QTc about 388 ms; the rhythm category is unchanged (no AF or flutter on either tracing) and the QTc difference is under 60 ms. Documented paroxysmal AF was captured on earlier tracings (2/26/2025 and 3/1/2025).

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm; discrete P wave about 120 ms before each QRS (PR approximately 115 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis +36 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. Single ECG on file, no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (348-650 ms) and no discrete P waves, only a fused T-P baseline. Mean ventricular rate 136 bpm, no measurable PR. QRS 100 ms, axis about 0 to +5 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 503 ms (over-corrected at this rate and poorly reproducible between leads because of the tachycardia). The prior ECG 107914094 from 2 hours earlier the same day also shows atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with the same QRS and, measured in the same lead (V2), an essentially identical QT; there is therefore no rhythm change and no reliable QTc change. Note that the same-day clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (regular 870-880 ms cycles) with one premature beat; PR 154 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis -25 (within the normal range), no bundle branch block. QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 432 ms. Prior ECG 104232242 (4/27/2025): sinus rhythm 61 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms - same rhythm and conduction, QTc change 31 ms (below threshold).

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF (PR about 105 ms, at the short end of normal). QRS 74 ms, frontal axis +1 (normal), no conduction block. QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +19 (normal), QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG on file and it pre-dates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, so it cannot serve as the post-start ECG.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (402-1152 ms) with absent organised P waves (pre-QRS segments correlate poorly between beats). Mean ventricular rate 70 bpm, no measurable PR. QRS 88 ms, axis +26 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 407 ms, Bazett QTc 441 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (11/12/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 168 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; the QTc change (+52 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, PR 106 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis +58 (normal), QT 424 ms with Bazett QTc 418 ms; no bundle branch block. The prior ECG 106045460 (3/8/2025) was essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 104 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 442 ms) - no significant change. This tracing pre-dates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start; a post-start ECG is due by 9/29/2026.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 138 ms, QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +51 (normal), QT 337 ms and Bazett QTc 397 ms. No conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +67 (normal), QT 391 ms, Bazett QTc 441 ms, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG 109048192 (2/2/2020) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QT 463 ms and QTc 516 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 75 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold (QTc decrease).

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, PR 156 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +40 (normal), QT 272 ms with Bazett QTc 386 ms. No conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (9/16/2016, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 92 ms, QTc 393 ms) the rhythm, intervals and axis are unchanged; QTc differs by only 7 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm with first-degree AV block: broad upright P waves in II with PR measured at 218 ms (P onset -258 ms, QRS onset -40 ms relative to the R peak). QRS 86 ms, axis +40 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms. Prior ECG 103042067 (11/30/2024): sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, PR about 190 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 378 ms; rhythm unchanged and QTc unchanged (the PR has lengthened slightly but that is not one of the reportable change categories).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at a mean 147 bpm: irregularly irregular RR intervals (312-604 ms), no organised P waves (pre-QRS correlation 0.33). No measurable PR. QRS 98 ms, axis -6 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 250 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 from the previous evening (9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with discrete P waves, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis +9 (normal), QT 352 ms with Bazett QTc 384 ms; no conduction abnormality. This matches the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm. The prior ECG 105362569 (11/21/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 71 bpm but with QT 494 ms and QTc 536 ms; the QTc has decreased by about 150 ms (QTc decrease >= 60 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (regular 805-820 ms cycles) with occasional ectopy; PR about 190 ms (upper normal), QRS 90 ms, axis +36 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms. Only ECG on file, no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm with well-formed P waves (100 microvolts in II) and PR 160 ms; QRS 94 ms, axis +40 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 291 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms. The prior ECG 102955795 (7/4/2022) showed sinus rhythm at 115 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 386 ms - no change. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history.

Underlying sinus rhythm at about 62-76 bpm (mean RR over the strip 794 ms) interrupted by a short run of irregular supraventricular ectopy in mid-tracing, consistent with her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation history. The conducted beats show broad P waves with PR measured at 198-206 ms (median 204 ms) - first-degree AV block. QRS 102 ms, axis -23 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. Only ECG on file.

Regular sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR 134 ms. QRS 92 ms, QT 351 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal QRS axis is about -175 degrees (deeply negative QRS in I and II with positive aVR), i.e. an extreme axis; the accompanying negative P wave in lead I raises the possibility of left/right arm lead reversal, which should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 104 ms, axis +40 (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT 489 ms, Bazett QTc 530 ms (patient on citalopram 40 mg daily). The prior ECG 107149156 (6/17/2020) showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc 418 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 100 ms (QTc increase >= 60 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis +54 (normal), QT 360 ms and Bazett QTc 384 ms; no conduction abnormality and no QT prolongation on escitalopram. Only ECG on file; it satisfies the required post-start ECG for escitalopram (started 2/12/2026).

Sinus bradycardia at 59 bpm with a single premature beat; PR 170 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis -8 (normal), QT 374 ms, Bazett QTc 372 ms, no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 108651109 (12/13/2018): sinus rhythm 66 bpm, PR 188 ms, QRS 108 ms, QTc 380 ms - no reportable change (QRS remains below 120 ms, QTc difference 8 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +45 (normal), no bundle branch block. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT 471 ms, Bazett QTc 502 ms. The prior ECG 100065910 (11/23/2022) had QTc 352 ms at 75 bpm, so the QTc has increased by about 150 ms - well beyond the 60 ms threshold - in the interval during which escitalopram was started. Flagged separately for QT safety review.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-456 ms, CV 0.02) with flutter waves at about 210 ms intervals (atrial rate near 285/min) that are negative in II/III/aVF and positive in V1 - typical atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. No measurable PR interval. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis +5 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT is difficult to define because flutter waves overlie the T wave; best estimate QT about 240 ms, Bazett QTc about 370 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (7/11/2022) showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves) at 107 bpm with QTc 418 ms, so the fibrillation has organised into flutter: resolved AF with new atrial flutter.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm; P wave onset about 195 ms and QRS onset about 50 ms before the R peak, giving a PR of roughly 140 ms (normal). QRS 102 ms, axis +19 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 359 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about 0 to -15 (normal), QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 406 ms, no conduction block. The prior ECG 102616671 (5/16/2021) showed sinus rhythm at 87 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 388 ms - no reportable change.

Sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with first-degree AV block (P onset -278 ms, QRS onset -62 ms relative to the R peak; PR about 215 ms) and left bundle branch block: QRS 132 ms with a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 and a deep rS/QS in V1-V3, with discordant T waves. Frontal axis -25 (normal). QT 428 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. The prior ECG 103686933 (6/3/2024) showed the same pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR 216 ms, QRS 132 ms LBBB, QTc 440 ms), so there is no change - the bundle branch block is not new.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +40 (normal), QT 331 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms, no conduction abnormality. The prior ECG 101016166 (3/18/2025) was essentially identical (101 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 430 ms) - no change.

Sinus rhythm at about 66-72 bpm (regular 905-925 ms cycles) with one premature ventricular couplet; PR 152 ms, QRS 90 ms, axis -26 (normal), QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm with frequent atrial/ventricular ectopy: dominant cycles are regular at about 1030 ms (58 bpm) with a consistent P wave at a PR of about 195 ms; mean ventricular rate across the 10-second strip is 71 bpm. QRS 90 ms, axis +20 (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged - QT 540 ms, Bazett QTc 585 ms - in a patient on amiodarone. The prior ECG 100867733 (4/6/2022) showed atrial fibrillation at 128 bpm (irregularly irregular, no organised P waves) with QTc 445 ms, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has risen by about 140 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +46 (normal), QT 302 ms, Bazett QTc 404 ms, no conduction abnormality. The prior ECG 107274479 (7/27/2019) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 417 ms - no reportable change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF and negative P in aVR, PR 114 ms. QRS 86 ms, axis +63 (normal), no conduction abnormality. QT 270 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 90 ms, axis +58 (normal), QT 314 ms and Bazett QTc 408 ms. No bundle branch block. Compared with ECG 102910502 recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (100 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 402 ms) there is no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis +33 (normal), QT 431 ms with Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. The prior ECG 104629882 (5/22/2023) showed sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QRS 90 ms and QTc 382 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc difference (18 ms) is not significant. Notably no atrial fibrillation is captured on either tracing despite the AF history.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 160 ms). QRS now 94 ms with only an rSR' remnant in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern), axis about +105 to +135 (right axis deviation; lead I net negative with near-isoelectric aVF). QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. The prior tracing 106516875 from earlier the same day (1:33 a.m., sinus rhythm 100 bpm) showed a complete right bundle branch block with QRS 150 ms and QTc 464 ms; the complete block is no longer present, i.e. the bundle branch block has resolved.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with one late-cycle ectopic beat; PR 164 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis +44 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 514 ms with Bazett QTc 538 ms - markedly prolonged (amiodarone started 11/10/2025). The prior ECG 108780865 (6/7/2025) showed a markedly irregular sinus-based rhythm at 63 bpm with QTc 473 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 65 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (388-1070 ms, mean 583 ms) with no consistent P waves and poor beat-to-beat correlation of the pre-QRS segment. Mean ventricular rate about 102 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 84 ms with a left frontal axis of about -45 degrees (negative in II/III/aVF). QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 491 ms (rate-corrected value inflated by the tachycardia and irregularity). This is the only ECG on file. The patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart entry needs correction and the rapid AF needs clinical review.

Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent; thrombocytopenia is documented but no bleeding event, so this needs prescriber review.

A current anticoagulant with a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review requires prescriber review.

Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are needed.
